Spotify Songs Analysis¶

Objective: Analyze the Spotify dataset to uncover trends in popularity, audio features, and genres using visualizations and insights.

In [23]:
#Analyze popularity

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Distribution of popularity
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.histplot(df['popularity'], bins=30, kde=True)
plt.title('Distribution of Track Popularity')
plt.xlabel('Popularity')
plt.ylabel('Number of Tracks')
plt.show()

Analytical Question: What is the distribution of track popularity?
Insight: Most tracks fall in the 40–70 range, meaning moderate popularity dominates; very few tracks are extremely popular or unpopular.

In [24]:
##Top 10 Artists by number of tracks
top_artists = df['artist_name'].value_counts().head(10)

plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.barplot(x=top_artists.values, y=top_artists.index)
plt.title('Top 10 Artists by Number of Tracks')
plt.xlabel('Number of Tracks')
plt.ylabel('Artist')
plt.show()

Analytical Question: Which artists have the most tracks in the dataset?
Insight: Artist(s) with the highest number of tracks are the most productive or consistently releasing music in the dataset.

In [25]:
#Danceability vs Popularity
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='danceability', y='popularity')
plt.title('Danceability vs Popularity')
plt.xlabel('Danceability')
plt.ylabel('Popularity')
plt.show()

Analytical Question: How does danceability relate to popularity?
Insight: Tracks with higher danceability tend to be slightly more popular, but the correlation is weak.

In [26]:
#Energy vs Loudness
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='energy', y='loudness')
plt.title('Energy vs Loudness')
plt.xlabel('Energy')
plt.ylabel('Loudness')
plt.show()

Analytical Question: Is there a relationship between a track’s energy and its loudness?
Insight: Higher energy tracks are generally louder, showing that energetic songs are often produced with more intensity.

In [27]:
#Correlation Heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(12,8))
sns.heatmap(df.corr(), annot=True, cmap='coolwarm')
plt.title('Correlation Between Numeric Features')
plt.show()

Analytical Question: How do numeric audio features correlate with each other?
Insight: Energy and loudness are strongly positively correlated; acousticness negatively correlates with loudness; valence shows moderate correlations with danceability.

In [16]:
top_valence = df.sort_values(by='valence', ascending=False).head(10)

plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.barplot(x='valence', y='track_name', data=top_valence)
plt.title('Top 10 Tracks by Valence (Happiness)')
plt.xlabel('Valence')
plt.ylabel('Track Name')
plt.show()

Analytical Question: Which tracks are the happiest (most positive)?
Insight: Tracks with the highest valence are the happiest; valence measures musical positivity.

#Tempo Distribution

sns.histplot(df['tempo'], bins=30, kde=True)
plt.title('Distribution of Track Tempo')
plt.xlabel('Tempo')
plt.ylabel('Number of Tracks')
plt.show()

Analytical Question: What is the distribution of track tempos?
Insight: Most songs have tempos between 80–120 BPM, which is typical for mainstream music.

In [29]:
#Popularity vs Acousticness
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='acousticness', y='popularity')
plt.title('Popularity vs Acousticness')
plt.xlabel('Acousticness')
plt.ylabel('Popularity')
plt.show()

Analytical Question: Does acousticness affect track popularity?
Insight: Tracks with higher acousticness tend to be slightly less popular, suggesting listeners favor more energetic or electronic sounds.

In [30]:
#Most Common Musical Keys
key_counts = df['key'].value_counts()

plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.barplot(x=key_counts.index, y=key_counts.values)
plt.title('Most Common Musical Keys')
plt.xlabel('Key')
plt.ylabel('Number of Tracks')
plt.show()

Analytical Question: Which keys are most frequently used in tracks?
Insight: Keys 0 (C) and 7 (G) are most common, indicating these keys are favored for composition.

In [31]:
#Top 10 Genres by Average Popularity
top_genres = df.groupby('genre')['popularity'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False).head(10)

plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.barplot(x=top_genres.values, y=top_genres.index)
plt.title('Top 10 Genres by Average Popularity')
plt.xlabel('Average Popularity')
plt.ylabel('Genre')
plt.show()

Analytical Question: Which genres have the highest average popularity?
Insight: Certain genres dominate in popularity (e.g., Pop or Hip-Hop), reflecting listener preferences in the dataset.
